title: The Two Laws of Reflection
description: Ray Bot aims a laser at Umbra's shifting mirrors. Predict exactly where it bounces using the two unbreakable laws of reflection — and the maze opens.

content.value: The angle of incidence (i) is always equal to the angle of reflection (r). If light hits a mirror at 30° to the normal, it bounces off at exactly 30° on the other side.

angle of incidence (i) = angle of reflection (r)

        \  i | r  /
         \   |   /
  ________\__|__/________   e.g. i = 40°  →  r = 40°
The incident ray, the reflected ray, and the normal all lie in the same plane. In other words, the whole reflection happens flat — the reflected ray never twists sideways out of the picture.

These two laws are true for EVERY reflecting surface — flat mirrors, curved mirrors, even a calm pond. Because the angles are always equal and predictable, engineers can aim light exactly where they want: in periscopes, telescopes, and even fibre-optic cables.
Memory trick: 'i = r'. If you know the angle light comes in at, you instantly know the angle it leaves at. They are always twins.
Key Takeaway: Law 1 — angle of incidence equals angle of reflection. Law 2 — the incident ray, reflected ray and normal all lie in one plane.

quiz.question: Light strikes a mirror at an angle of incidence of 35°. What is the angle of reflection?
quiz.explain: By the first law of reflection, the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence — so it is also 35°.

quiz.question: The first law of reflection states that…
options: light always bends toward the normal
the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection
light slows down in a mirror
quiz.explain: The first law: angle of incidence (i) = angle of reflection (r), both measured from the normal.

quiz.question: According to the second law, the incident ray, reflected ray and normal…
options: all lie in the same plane
point in three different directions in space
are always at 90° to each other
quiz.explain: The second law says all three lie in one plane — the reflection stays flat and does not twist sideways.
